  1. Alabama · State constitutions and referenda · State and city finance, Feb. 16Constitutional amendment election, nineteen amendments, most of them county taxes and fees.   1. Districting and apportionment, Jan. 10California · workdayEisenhower transmits the Census Director’s statement under 2 U.S.C. § 2a: each State’s population and its Representatives, 435 by the method of equal proportions. For the 88th Congress: California from 30 to 38, Florida 8 to 12; Arizona, Hawaii, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, Ohio and Texas one more each. Pennsylvania from 30 to 27; Arkansas, Massachusetts and New York two fewer; Alabama, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maine, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, North Carolina and West Virginia one. The Senior Citizens Committee, some eighty, called by Smyer: Sheriff Bailey, the police at the breaking point; Marshall, for a negotiated peace. They authorize the merchants’ negotiators, two or three dissenting.1 That night Smyer, Vann and two merchants with Pitts, Shores and Andrew Young, Marshall present: the stores desegregated, jobs upgraded, a biracial committee;2 the release of the jailed unsettled.3

Friday, Jan. 15
  1. King · Civil rights: the executive, Jan. 15the LBJ Ranch · 12:06 p.m.Johnson, at the Ranch, and King by telephone.1 King urges Whitney Young for a Cabinet post. The FBI overhears.2 Johnson gives birthday greetings, King’s thirty-sixth, and asks for recommendations on pending appointments.3 King asks that the first Negro be named to the Cabinet; Johnson says he plans to. Johnson presses the Medicare, education and poverty bills and, to King’s surprise, says they must “come up with” voting rights legislation: “That will answer 70 percent of your problems!”4 Johnson would have age and literacy the only tests and no poll tax, and, if the States fail, registration under federal control: “They can all go to the Post Office like they buy a stamp.”5 Johnson: voting rights “will be the greatest breakthrough of anything not even excepting this ’64 act.”6 On the education bills Johnson says: “We’ve got to try with every force at our command.”7 King says the five Southern States Johnson did not carry have under 40 percent of Negroes registered.8

March 1965

Monday, Mar. 1
  1. Voting rights: Selma · Alabama · King, Mar. 1A registration day. Selma: King leads some 300 to the Dallas County courthouse in the rain; Clark keeps them outside; 266 complete applications, twice the record. Camden, Wilcox County: ten of some 200 in line allowed to apply.
